text.p: Italian BTP futures opened slightly higher then quickly slipped back in line with losses in German bunds and so continued the lower trend from Thursday's BTP futures trading session, dealers said.
Sentiment was dampened after retail customers in the U.S. shunned Thursday's 30-year bond auction, the third and final leg of the quarterly refunding, and T-bonds ended lower overnight.

"There is little fresh news to move the market, but the overall tone to bond markets does seem to be negative this morning," said one LIFFE dealer. The cash market after opening gains also slipped back into negative territory.
Official data showing Italian industrial production in June registered a month-on-month 0.4 percent rise had little market impact, dealers said.

Bundesbank council member Ernest Welteke said in a radio interview that the German central bank would not touch interest rate as long as there were no signs of inflationary pressures. This helped support bunds at lower levels and could help stabilise BTPs, dealers said.
